# 周易鄭康成註

**ID:** KR1a0003
**Custom ID:** ZB1a0002
**Date (file):** 2015-09-12 00:39:40.790024
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V7.2, p129
**Extent:** 1 卷
**Base edition:** SBCK

## Authors / Editors
- 鄭玄 (漢朝) 撰 127 - 200
- 王應麟 (宋朝) 編

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-*juàn* reconstruction by the late-Sòng polymath [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) Wáng Yīnglín of [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán's lost *Zhōuyì zhù* 周易註, the most authoritative of the Hàn *xiàngshù* 象數 commentaries. Zhèng's original was in nine (or ten) *juàn* and was the foundational alternative to the *yìlǐ* 義理 reading later canonised by [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì ([KR1a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0006)); it was already in fragmentary state by the Northern Sòng and effectively lost during the Sòng. Wáng Yīnglín gathered the surviving fragments from [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò's *Zhōuyì jíjiě* 周易集解 ([KR1a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0008)), [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* 經典釋文, the *Shī* 詩 and Three-Rites *zhèngyì* 正義, the *Chūnqiū* 春秋 commentaries, the *Hòu Hànshū* 後漢書, and [李善](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%96%84) Lǐ Shàn's *Wénxuǎn* 文選 commentary, and arranged them under hexagram heads following the received *Zhōuyì* sequence. It is the earliest systematic *jíyì* 輯佚 ("recompilation of lost texts") of Zhèng's *Yì* and the parent text for the further-augmented [KR1a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0004) *Zēngbǔ Zhèng shì Zhōuyì* 增補鄭氏周易 of [惠棟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%A0%E6%A3%9F) Huì Dòng.

The catalog assigns the dynasty as Hàn (the dynasty of the source author), but the actual composition window is the late Southern Sòng: notBefore 1241 (Wáng Yīnglín's *jìnshì* date and the start of his serious bibliographic productivity) — notAfter 1296 (his death). The Sìkù editors note in the *tiyao* that, when a work is wholly a recompilation of an earlier author, the convention is to file it under the original author's dynasty regardless.

**Abstract**

[鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán (127–200), of Běihǎi Gāomì 北海高密 (modern Shāndōng), was the last and greatest of the Hàn classicists, equally authoritative on the *Yì*, *Shī*, *Sānlǐ*, *Lúnyǔ*, and *Xiàojīng*. His *Zhōuyì zhù* synthesised the Mèng-Jīng *xiàngshù* tradition (received via [第五元先](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AC%AC%E4%BA%94%E5%85%83%E5%85%88) Dìwǔ Yuánxiān) with the older [費直](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B2%BB%E7%9B%B4) Fèi Zhí line received via [馬融](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E8%9E%8D) Mǎ Róng. The commentary made central use of *hùtǐ* 互體 ("interlocked-body" hexagrams generated by lines 2-3-4 and 3-4-5), of *guàqì* 卦氣 ("hexagram-breath" calendrical correlations), and of philological glossing — methods later marginalised by [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì but central to Hàn *Yì* hermeneutics.

The *Suíshū jīngjí zhì* records the original at nine *juàn*. By the early Táng both Zhèng's and Wáng's commentaries were officially canonised side by side; [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) Kǒng Yǐngdá chose Wáng for his *Zhōuyì zhèngyì* 周易正義 ([KR1a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0007)), which became the imperial standard, and Zhèng's text gradually fell out of circulation. [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò's *Zhōuyì jíjiě* (mid-Táng, [KR1a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0008)) preserves the largest single block of Zhèng quotations; [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* preserves a smaller but textually crucial set. The Sòng *Chóngwén zǒngmù* (1042) still records "1 *juàn*" surviving — covering only the four "Wing" texts *Wényán*, *Xùguà*, *Shuōguà*, and *Záguà* — and the *Zhōngxīng shūmù* (Southern Sòng) records nothing.

[王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) Wáng Yīnglín (1223–1296), of Qìngyuán 慶元 (modern Níngbō 寧波), was the leading bibliographer and *kǎojù* 考據 scholar of the late Southern Sòng, *jìnshì* of 1241 and *bóxué hóngcí* of 1256. His other surviving compilations include the *Yùhǎi* 玉海, *Kùnxué jìwén* 困學紀聞, and *Sānzìjīng* 三字經 (traditionally attributed). For the present work he combed Lǐ Dǐngzuò, Lù Démíng, the *Shī* and *Sānlǐ zhèngyì*, and the *Hòu Hànshū* and *Wénxuǎn* commentaries, organised the surviving fragments under hexagram heads, and appended a separately-grouped tail-section of unattributable fragments together with eight illustrative *hùtǐ* citations from the *Zuǒzhuàn*, *Lǐjì*, and *Zhōulǐ* sub-commentaries. The compilation was substantially complete by the late thirteenth century; it is the earliest extant systematic *jíyì* 輯佚 reconstruction of a Hàn *Yì* commentary, and it became the model for the Qīng evidential reconstructions that followed.

The Qīng *kǎozhèng* scholar [惠棟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%A0%E6%A3%9F) Huì Dòng (1697–1758) produced an enlarged and textually corrected version, *Zēngbǔ Zhèng shì Zhōuyì* 增補鄭氏周易 (= [KR1a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0004)); the Sìkù editors record both, citing Yīnglín's pioneering role.
